answer:
The debate began 2018-04-03 (thread t1081) when Robert Sanderson proposed renaming the gender-marked classes E22 Man-Made Object, E24 Physical Man-Made Thing, E25 Man-Made Feature and E71 Man-Made Thing. His email laid out the options: (1) simply drop 'Man-' and keep 'Made' (E22 Made Object, E25 Made Feature, E24 Physical Made Thing); (2) use 'Artificial'/'Artifact' (E22 Artifact, E25 Artificial Feature, E71 Artificial Thing); (3) 'Produced' (fits with the Production class but felt less obvious); and worse-rated alternatives 'Synthetic' (odd for natural materials), 'Manufactured' (implies industrial machinery), 'Constructed'/'Built' (implies large structures like buildings/roads). Athanasios Velios supported dropping 'Man-' and noted the issue is specific to English (other languages, e.g. Greek, don't have the problem).

The issue was revived 2019-04-12 (thread t1194), again by Robert Sanderson on behalf of the Linked Art consortium, as a formal proposal: primary choice 'Made' (Made Object/Made Feature/Made Thing), secondary choice 'Human-Made'. Objections and concerns raised in the ensuing discussion: Pierre Choffé and Franco Niccolucci argued the 'bias' was an English-specific etymological quirk and objected to the effort/cost of change (calling it 'political correctness'); Richard Light and George Bruseker raised the technical/cost concern that existing data with old URIs/labels would become inconsistent; George Bruseker and Franco Niccolucci noted 'Made' alone is ambiguous (e.g., a cat could 'make' a scratch), favoring 'Human-Made' despite it being more of a mouthful; Christian-Emil Smith Ore checked the OED to confirm 'made' wasn't overly broad; Martin Doerr stayed personally opposed, arguing 'Man-Made' was an established, useful term and that language change doesn't address real gender equity, but did not block the process and offered to run the vote; 'Artificial' had already been considered and rejected earlier because of its 'insincere/affected' secondary meaning.

On 2019-04-16 Robert Sanderson noted general consensus had shifted toward 'Human-Made' and asked to move to a vote. Martin Doerr issued a formal vote 2019-04-24 in thread t1196 ('PLEASE VOTE: Issue Man-Made'): "The proposal is to replace in all CRM labels 'Man-Made' by 'Human-Made'." Multiple SIG members (Robert Sanderson, Tony Gill, Maximilian Schich, Maja Žumer, Дарья Юрьевна Гук, and others) voted YES with no NO votes found in the retrieved messages. The ontology entry for E22 (search.py concept E22) confirms the adopted outcome: the current (v7.1.3) label is 'E22 Human-Made Object', i.e. the standards body adopted 'Human-Made' rather than plain 'Made' or 'Artificial'.
queries_run: search "Man-Made Object remove Man class label" -k 10
notes: The 2018 thread (t1081) is where the option set (Made, Artificial/Artifact, Produced, Synthetic, Manufactured, Constructed/Built) was actually enumerated; the 2019 thread (t1194) reframed it as a binary choice (Made vs Human-Made) and thread t1196 held the formal vote. search.py concept E22's chronology correctly flagged t1194 and t1196 as 'decided', which routed me straight to the resolution. No NO votes were found in retrieved messages, but I cannot rule out that some exist outside the top hits returned.
